{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Extend the existing Spring XD stream deployment, Kafka source, message-bus, module, and configuration abstractions rather than introducing a parallel runtime model.",
    "Represent a Kafka source starting offset as deployment-time stream configuration, supporting replay from an explicit offset while preserving committed progress during normal module crashes.",
    "Use Kafka consumer partition assignment and explicit offset seeking during deployment; treat an explicitly supplied deployment offset as taking precedence over previously committed offsets for that deployment.",
    "Persist or commit Kafka progress through the existing Kafka consumer and message-bus mechanisms so that module crashes do not lose progress for a running stream.",
    "Implement Kafka partition pre-allocation as deterministic assignment of topic partitions to source instances at deployment time, with validation for partition-count and instance-count mismatches.",
    "Implement message-bus node pre-allocation using deterministic ownership metadata supplied by the stream deployment coordinator, while retaining recovery behavior for crashed or redeployed containers.",
    "Implement reactor-stream as a processor module with configurable time windows and field/expression evaluation, initially supporting the documented min and average operations.",
    "Implement microbatching as a source-to-downstream delivery batching option controlled by a batch interval, with bounded buffering and flush behavior on interval expiry.",
    "Treat Spark work as a bounded investigation and proof of concept that evaluates integration architecture, serialization, deployment, and operational constraints rather than a production Spark integration.",
    "Use automated unit and integration tests with embedded or containerized Kafka where practical, and document externally managed infrastructure requirements for performance testing.",
    "Update the project wiki with configuration, deployment, operational, examples, limitations, and troubleshooting information for all delivered features."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "A usable Spring XD codebase, build, test framework, Kafka integration, message bus, deployment coordinator, and module framework already exist.",
    "The increment is implemented by one experienced Java developer familiar with Spring, Kafka, distributed messaging, and the existing Spring XD codebase.",
    "The specification does not define exact APIs or persistence details, so backward-compatible configuration extensions and existing framework conventions are used.",
    "Kafka broker and client versions are compatible with the existing project, and no broker-side feature requiring a separate upgrade is included.",
    "The starting offset requirement covers numeric offsets per Kafka partition; timestamp-based offsets, arbitrary offset ranges, and a new administrative user interface are excluded.",
    "The unresolved semantics for undeploying and redeploying without a specific offset are handled by retaining existing committed progress; an explicitly supplied offset causes replay from that offset.",
    "Partition pre-allocation targets one stream deployment and does not attempt to solve arbitrary dynamic scaling without redeployment.",
    "Crash recovery must preserve progress for a running stream, but exactly-once processing semantics are not assumed; existing at-least-once delivery behavior remains.",
    "The reactor-stream module supports the documented time-window use case and a small initial expression set; a complete general-purpose Reactor DSL is excluded.",
    "Microbatching supports interval-based batching as shown in the example; size-based batching, cross-stream transactions, and end-to-end exactly-once guarantees are excluded.",
    "The Spark activity produces a documented POC and recommendation, not a production-ready Spark Streaming module.",
    "Performance infrastructure work covers provisioning and repeatable benchmark scripts/configuration on Rackspace or an equivalent environment; cloud account, network, and hardware costs are external.",
    "Wiki publication access and an existing documentation structure are available.",
    "Effort includes implementation, code review by self, automated tests, integration troubleshooting, and developer documentation, but excludes project management and elapsed waiting time."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Increment analysis and technical design",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing stream deployment, Kafka source, message bus, module lifecycle, configuration, checkpointing, and testing architecture; define compatible APIs, deployment state, failure behavior, and implementation sequencing for U2 through U8.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Kafka starting-offset support",
      "activity_description": "Add deployment configuration and runtime handling for explicit per-partition starting offsets, implement offset seeking and precedence over committed offsets, preserve normal progress across module crashes, validate invalid offsets, and add unit and integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Kafka source partition pre-allocation",
      "activity_description": "Implement deterministic partition allocation among Kafka source modules at stream deployment, pass assignments to consumers, prevent unintended rebalancing during normal deployment, handle assignment changes and failures, and test multiple topics, partition counts, and module counts.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Message-bus node partition pre-allocation",
      "activity_description": "Extend message-bus deployment and container coordination to pre-assign stream partitions or channels to nodes, maintain ownership metadata, define crash and redeployment recovery behavior, and test stable allocation and failover scenarios.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Reactor-stream processor module",
      "activity_description": "Create the reactor-stream processor module, implement configurable time-window grouping and field-path extraction, support initial min and average expressions, integrate module lifecycle and stream configuration, provide examples, and add unit and end-to-end tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 18
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Microbatching capability",
      "activity_description": "Add interval-based buffering and flush behavior to the applicable source or messaging path, expose batchInterval configuration, define empty and shutdown flush semantics, preserve error handling and back-pressure behavior, and test throughput-oriented and failure cases.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Spark investigation and proof of concept",
      "activity_description": "Investigate Spark Streaming integration options, create a narrowly scoped POC using representative Spring XD input and output, evaluate deployment, serialization, latency, fault tolerance, and operational implications, and document the recommended design and remaining work.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Performance testing infrastructure",
      "activity_description": "Provision or configure the Rackspace-based benchmark environment, automate installation and startup of required services, create Kafka baseline and initial Spring XD benchmark scenarios, capture repeatable metrics, and document execution and teardown procedures.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration and regression testing",
      "activity_description": "Run full build and regression suites, add deployment-level scenarios combining offsets, partition allocation, crash recovery, reactor-stream, and microbatching, diagnose integration failures, and verify compatibility with existing stream behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Wiki documentation and release readiness",
      "activity_description": "Publish configuration reference, deployment examples, operational semantics, offset and redeployment behavior, partition allocation guidance, reactor-stream and microbatching examples, Spark POC findings, performance-test instructions, and known limitations.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 121
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Extend the existing Spring XD stream deployment, Kafka source, message-bus, module, and configuration abstractions rather than introducing a parallel runtime model.
Represent a Kafka source starting offset as deployment-time stream configuration, supporting replay from an explicit offset while preserving committed progress during normal module crashes.

Use Kafka consumer partition assignment and explicit offset seeking during deployment; treat an explicitly supplied deployment offset as taking precedence over previously committed offsets for that deployment.
Persist or commit Kafka progress through the existing Kafka consumer and message-bus mechanisms so that module crashes do not lose progress for a running stream.
Implement Kafka partition pre-allocation as deterministic assignment of topic partitions to source instances at deployment time, with validation for partition-count and instance-count mismatches.
Implement message-bus node pre-allocation using deterministic ownership metadata supplied by the stream deployment coordinator, while retaining recovery behavior for crashed or redeployed containers.
Implement reactor-stream as a processor module with configurable time windows and field/expression evaluation, initially supporting the documented min and average operations.
Implement microbatching as a source-to-downstream delivery batching option controlled by a batch interval, with bounded buffering and flush behavior on interval expiry.

Treat Spark work as a bounded investigation and proof of concept that evaluates integration architecture, serialization, deployment, and operational constraints rather than a production Spark integration.
Use automated unit and integration tests with embedded or containerized Kafka where practical, and document externally managed infrastructure requirements for performance testing.
Update the project wiki with configuration, deployment, operational, examples, limitations, and troubleshooting information for all delivered features.
assumptions: A usable Spring XD codebase, build, test framework, Kafka integration, message bus, deployment coordinator, and module framework already exist.
The increment is implemented by one experienced Java developer familiar with Spring, Kafka, distributed messaging, and the existing Spring XD codebase.
The specification does not define exact APIs or persistence details, so backward-compatible configuration extensions and existing framework conventions are used.
Kafka broker and client versions are compatible with the existing project, and no broker-side feature requiring a separate upgrade is included.
The starting offset requirement covers numeric offsets per Kafka partition; timestamp-based offsets, arbitrary offset ranges, and a new administrative user interface are excluded.
The unresolved semantics for undeploying and redeploying without a specific offset are handled by retaining existing committed progress; an explicitly supplied offset causes replay from that offset.
Partition pre-allocation targets one stream deployment and does not attempt to solve arbitrary dynamic scaling without redeployment.
Crash recovery must preserve progress for a running stream, but exactly-once processing semantics are not assumed; existing at-least-once delivery behavior remains.
The reactor-stream module supports the documented time-window use case and a small initial expression set; a complete general-purpose Reactor DSL is excluded.
Microbatching supports interval-based batching as shown in the example; size-based batching, cross-stream transactions, and end-to-end exactly-once guarantees are excluded.
The Spark activity produces a documented POC and recommendation, not a production-ready Spark Streaming module.
Performance infrastructure work covers provisioning and repeatable benchmark scripts/configuration on Rackspace or an equivalent environment; cloud account, network, and hardware costs are external.
Wiki publication access and an existing documentation structure are available.
Effort includes implementation, code review by self, automated tests, integration troubleshooting, and developer documentation, but excludes project management and elapsed waiting time.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing stream deployment, Kafka source, message bus, module lifecycle, configuration, checkpointing, and testing architecture; define compatible APIs, deployment state, failure behavior, and implementation sequencing for U2 through U8.

Add deployment configuration and runtime handling for explicit per-partition starting offsets, implement offset seeking and precedence over committed offsets, preserve normal progress across module crashes, validate invalid offsets, and add unit and integration tests.

Implement deterministic partition allocation among Kafka source modules at stream deployment, pass assignments to consumers, prevent unintended rebalancing during normal deployment, handle assignment changes and failures, and test multiple topics, partition counts, and module counts.

Extend message-bus deployment and container coordination to pre-assign stream partitions or channels to nodes, maintain ownership metadata, define crash and redeployment recovery behavior, and test stable allocation and failover scenarios.

Create the reactor-stream processor module, implement configurable time-window grouping and field-path extraction, support initial min and average expressions, integrate module lifecycle and stream configuration, provide examples, and add unit and end-to-end tests.

Add interval-based buffering and flush behavior to the applicable source or messaging path, expose batchInterval configuration, define empty and shutdown flush semantics, preserve error handling and back-pressure behavior, and test throughput-oriented and failure cases.
